editorial.headline: Household Heat Appliances With a Clear Bali PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27520 covers the manufacture of household electrothermal appliances, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27520 is the industrial home of household electrothermal equipment: appliances that turn electricity into domestic heat, cooking, drying, ironing, brewing, roasting, grilling, warming, or extraction. The record’s scope is concrete rather than abstract. It includes electric water-heating devices for cooking, electric blankets, hair-care appliances such as dryers, combs, brushes, and curlers, electric irons, room heaters, electric ovens, microwave ovens, cookers, hot plates, toasters, coffee and tea makers, fry pans, roasters, electric grills, kitchen hoods, and electric heating-resistor equipment. In plain English, this is not general electronics and not every appliance factory. It is the manufacturing category for household heat-based electrical products.

The boundary is equally important. The slim record excludes commercial refrigerators and freezers, air conditioners, attic fans, permanent room heaters, commercial ventilation fans or exhaust fans, commercial cooking equipment, commercial laundry and dry-cleaning equipment, commercial vacuum cleaners, and similar equipment for business or commercial use. That exclusion keeps the code focused on household electrothermal manufacturing, not the broader universe of commercial machinery or institutional equipment. For a founder, the useful test is whether the intended product is a domestic electrothermal appliance of the kind named in the scope, rather than a commercial-grade system or facility-oriented machine.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not framed only as a large industrial play in the slim record; it can sit across the full stated scale range. A small maker of household heating appliances and a larger manufacturer of electric ovens, hoods, or heating-resistor products are still dealing with the same activity description, provided the product remains inside the household electrothermal scope. The editorial point is not that every factory is simple to set up, but that the KBLI record itself does not narrow the registration scale to one class of operator.

The national-versus-Bali picture is clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced in the record to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali then adds the test that often changes the answer for foreign founders: the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the record does not mark the code as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest conclusion is therefore direct: this activity is foreign-open nationally and, on the slim record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.
